stories.headline: Michael Carrick to lead Man United vs. Chelsea amid uncertain future - sources
stories.summary: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick took training on Tuesday and now expects to be in charge against Chelsea on Saturday, sources have told ESPN.
stories.body:
Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick took training on Tuesday and now expects to be in charge against Chelsea on Saturday, sources have told ESPN, amid continuing uncertainty surrounding his long-term future at Old Trafford.

Carrick arrived at United's training base just before 8 a.m. The first-team playing squad also reported back after being given a day off on Monday.

The 45-year-old led the session, which started at 11 a.m., as United prepare for Chelsea.

- Transfer rumors, news: PSG eye Man United wonderkid Gabriel

- Man United are in crisis (again), but where are the Glazers?

- Real Madrid best Barça in brilliant Clásico; Man United mess deepens; Spurs win again

The expectation is that Carrick will be in the dug-out at Stamford Bridge with the opportunity to turn the situation around, sources told ESPN.

It did not go unnoticed by the United front office that Carrick received significant support from United fans during and after the defeat to Bournemouth -- with most of the frustration directed at the players, sources told ESPN.

Players were booed at the final whistle and then fiercely as they followed Carrick down the tunnel on a day when the manager left skipper Bruno Fernandes on the bench.

The 32-year-old, who also arrived at Carrington on Tuesday morning, has been a pale imitation of the player who won end-of-season awards having set a new Premier League assist record, with the frustrated captain questioning the manager's tactics in Como. Carrick claimed the decision to name him among the substitutes on Sunday was a "pure football" decision rather than punishment but the Portugal international did not play a minute.

Fernandes was at Carrington to for pre-planned treatment on Monday and social media users spotted his Instagram account liked a video that had written above it "never push a loyal person to the point where they no longer care."

Carrick was also at Carrington on Monday afternoon to watch United's Under-21s play in a behind closed doors friendly.

CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox arrived earlier in the day to hold talks in the wake of the 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth.

Carrick remains under severe pressure after a run of eight games without a win.

United have won just once in the Premier League this season -- against newly promoted Ipswich at Old Trafford in August -- and sit 16th in the table, one point above the relegation zone.

The visit to Chelsea on Saturday kicks off a difficult run of fixtures for United.

They face back-to-back home games against AS Roma and Aston Villa next week before the November international break.

The first game back after the international fixtures is against Liverpool at Anfield on Nov. 22.

With United making their worst ever start to a Premier League season, winning just one league game since the start of the campaign, Carrick had been expected to lose his job with the club hierarchy exploring potential replacements including Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte, sources told ESPN.

Press Association contributed to this report.

stories.headline: NBA season 2026-27: Best and worst from the first week
stories.summary: Our insiders break down standout moments and answer the biggest questions from the first days of the NBA season.
stories.body:
Plenty of intriguing storylines have emerged just one week into the 2026-27 NBA season.

The defending Eastern and Western Conference champions have been shaky to begin their title defenses. The reigning NBA champion New York Knicks started the season 0-3 amid ring night drama, while the San Antonio Spurs dropped games against the Houston Rockets and Oklahoma City Thunder before recording their first win against the Dallas Mavericks, who were without Rookie of the Year Cooper Flagg, on Saturday.

Their struggles have allowed other contenders to take center stage, such as Luka Doncic putting up 52 points against the Utah Jazz on Sunday en route to a 3-0 start for the Los Angeles Lakers. Injuries have already started to take their toll, too. The Detroit Pistons' Jalen Duren, the Orlando Magic's Jalen Suggs and the Thunder's Jalen Williams all suffered injuries during opening week that will sideline them, with Williams being stretchered off the court.

Our analysts looked at what has surprised them the most so far, some bold predictions for the rest of the season and which newcomer made the best first impression. Then, our reporters answered the biggest questions facing 12 title contenders based on ESPN's Basketball Power Index, which projects every team's chances of making the 2027 NBA Finals.

Let's break down the best and worst moments from opening week.

Note: BPI chances account for games through the morning on Monday, Oct. 26.

Jump to a contender question:

BOS | CLE | DEN | DET

HOU | LAL | MIN | NY

OKC | PHI | SA | TOR

What has surprised you most so far?
Bobby Marks: There is still a lot of basketball left this season, but Memphis has already stood out in the first week.

The Grizzlies followed their strong preseason (3-1) with regular-season wins at home against the Utah Jazz and on the road against the Golden State Warriors and Sacramento Kings. Memphis' 3-0 record after opening week is its best start since the 2017-18 season.

Early-season success can be attributed to guard Ty Jerome, who appeared in only 15 games last season, and highly touted rookie Cameron Boozer. In the first three games, Jerome has scored 45, 28 and 31 points. The 104 points trail only Ja Morant for the most points in Grizzlies history through the first three games. In the win at Sacramento, Boozer became the fifth player (Ben Simmons, Oscar Robertson, Elgin Baylor and Maurice Stokes) in NBA history with at least 10 rebounds and four assists in their first three games.

From a team perspective, Memphis is winning games on the boards and with extra possessions. The Grizzlies rank first in offensive rebound percentage, second in offensive rebounds and third in second-chance points.

Overall, it's a surprising start to the season for a team that ranked 24th in ESPN's Basketball Power Index before the season.

Ben Golliver: Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs didn't lose consecutive games after the All-Star break last season, so it was jarring to see them open this season with losses to the Thunder and Rockets.

Oklahoma City squeezed the life out of San Antonio's offense, holding Wembanyama to 1-of-13 (7.7%) shooting -- easily the worst shooting performance of his four-year career. Spurs coach Mitch Johnson also deployed a four-guard starting lineup that couldn't slow down Shai Gilgeous-Alexander or reliably convert when dared to shoot from outside.

Wembanyama found more success against Houston, but the 7-foot-4 center had a potential game-tying basket stuffed at the rim by 6-7 guard Amen Thompson. After blowing lead after lead to the Knicks in the 2026 NBA Finals, the Spurs' late-game offense and Wembanyama's decision-making in clutch situations will be scrutinized all season. The early returns have been concerning for a young team with championship aspirations.

Zach Kram: I initially planned to write my answer about Mario Hezonja, who has played a much larger role than expected in Cleveland. The former No. 5 pick averaged 9.5 points in 19.5 minutes in his first two games after a six-year absence from the NBA.

But then the Knicks lost at home against Orlando to fall to 0-3 after close defeats against Philadelphia and Boston. New York has lost as many games in a week as it did during the 2026 playoffs!

One rotten week shouldn't cause real concern about New York's longer-term chances to repeat; after all, the team was frustratingly inconsistent throughout last season, as well, before finally finding its rhythm in the playoffs.

But if you squint, there are a few early warning signs worth monitoring. Mikal Bridges is averaging only 3.3 PPG on 22% shooting, and the bench hasn't been as helpful as it was during the Knicks' title run. Those trends need to change for the Knicks to reclaim their place atop the Eastern Conference.

What's the one contract situation fans should keep a close eye on?
Marks: There are actually three players we should focus on.

The first two are Tyrese Maxey and Anthony Edwards. Both players are under contract for the next three seasons, but have significant financial implications for the future. If Maxey and Edwards are named MVP or All-NBA (there is also the criteria for Defensive Player of the Year), then either player is eligible to sign a four-year, $304 million supermax extension next summer, with the first year of the deal beginning in 2029-30.

Through the first week of the season, Maxey (28.8 PPG) and Edwards (28.7 PPG) rank in the top 10 in points per game. Maxey trails only Jamal Murray, Nikola Jokic and Zach LaVine in minutes per game.

The other player to watch is LaVine. On an expiring $49 million contract, LaVine ranks third in points per game (29 PPG) for the winless Kings. If he has a strong season and Sacramento continues to sit at the bottom of the standings, will there be a trade market for him closer to the February deadline?

Because LaVine's salary is more than the $15 million non-tax midlevel exception, teams over the first and second apron are not allowed to sign him if he were bought out of his contract. That eliminates the Denver Nuggets, Warriors, Knicks, Magic, Minnesota Timberwolves, Thunder and Phoenix Suns from signing LaVine.

Which newcomer made the best first impression?
Golliver: LaMelo Ball has delivered a much-needed breath of fresh air to the Timberwolves, who appear happier and less burdened than during a string of frustrating postseason exits. Though Ball's scoring has been hit or miss, his presence as a creator has paid immediate dividends for franchise guard Edwards, who torched the Heat for 45 points in the season opener.

Despite his phenomenal talent, Edwards' turnover issues, streaky outside shooting and lack of stamina have contributed to Minnesota's past playoff struggles. Ball can help with all those issues. Edwards should be spared from some playmaking duties, benefit from higher-quality looks and encounter fewer double-teams thanks to Ball, who can make aggressive defenses pay with his range, driving ability and passing instincts.

Minnesota sacrificed frontcourt depth and physicality to acquire Ball, but forwards Jaden McDaniels and Jonathan Kuminga boast good athleticism and enough size to support center Rudy Gobert. Thanks largely to Ball's impact, the new-look Timberwolves have been significantly more watchable to open the new season.

What's a bold prediction you'd like to make after seeing a week of games?
Kram: Golden State will win fewer than 30 games. Coming off a 37-win campaign, the Warriors didn't have the highest expectations this season due to injuries and a quiet summer -- but they've failed to meet even that low bar in the early going. The Warriors are 0-3, and on Sunday, they started a lineup that looked like a group you'd see in the second half of a preseason game: Brandon Williams, Gui Santos, Will Richard, Yaxel Lendeborg and Graham Ike.

Lendeborg has been one of the best rookies so far, but the Warriors have little size, little scoring outside Stephen Curry -- and little chance of contending for a playoff spot.

More questions for contenders

Boston Celtics
BPI chances to make the Finals: 22.6%

Are the Celtics living well without Jaylen Brown?

This will be the perpetual question throughout the season and likely won't be settled until it's over. Don't worry, Brown isn't interested in letting the topic go anyway. Jayson Tatum is off to an uneven start: He has played one great game, one bad game and one average game, which was Monday night in a demolition of the Chicago Bulls.

Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla is leaning into depth, playing 11-man rotations and sticking to his philosophy of bombing away from 3-point range. So far, Paul George is making 50% of his long-range attempts, which will largely define how his season is viewed. He's overpaid, yes, but the Celtics didn't pay him, and they traded for him to be plugged in as a supporting piece, not a cornerstone. They also need Mitchell Robinson -- signed to be an elite offensive rebounder and good defender -- to fill a role, though he's off to a bit of a slow start.

There's no gray area when judging Payton Pritchard's start. Back to his sixth-man job full time, Pritchard is off to a strong start after recently signing a contract extension. He had 28 points against the Bulls, showing off his lightning-fast scoring ability, which is being counted on to fill some of the offensive void left by Brown's departure. -- Brian Windhorst

Cleveland Cavaliers
BPI chances to make the Finals: 5.5%

Is there anything different about this Cavs team?

The Cavs' first game of the season looked a lot like the last time we saw them. They led by 29 points on opening night against Philadelphia, primed to make a statement about being overlooked among the contenders in the East. And then ... Cleveland became the first team in league history to blow a 20-point lead after halftime on opening night.

It mirrored Cleveland's epic collapse during Game 1 of the conference finals -- when the Cavs were up 22 points against New York but collapsed down the stretch and got swept out of the playoffs. So, are the Cavs truly an under-the-radar contender? Or will they keep running into the same wall, despite winning at least 48 games in three of the past four seasons? -- Jamal Collier

Denver Nuggets
BPI chances to make the Finals: 3.2%

Where else can the Nuggets find some depth on the roster?

The Nuggets are paying a combined $187 million to their starting lineup, leaving little for the reserves. Those financial restraints led them to a summer trade of Peyton Watson to Cleveland for a draft pick and no players in return, creating a larger need on the wing.

DeMar DeRozan arrived on a veteran minimum contract and has been productive in his first week in Denver, scoring 25 combined in 52 minutes. But the first-week revelation has been Trevon Brazile, the rookie the Nuggets drafted No. 35 out of Arkansas. In a frantic overtime win over the New Orleans Pelicans, Brazile made a handful of spectacular plays down the stretch, including two huge putbacks, a crucial steal in the final minute of regulation, a pair of leaping blocks on attempted 3s and a massive corner 3 to seal it. Denver's decreased depth won't feel as drastic an issue if Brazile continues to pop. -- Anthony Slater

Detroit Pistons
BPI chances to make the Finals: 23.8%

How will the Pistons handle being without Jalen Duren and Ausar Thompson?

Thompson should be back sooner than Duren, and Thompson is critically important to Detroit's stingy defense as arguably the league's best wing defender. Ron Holland II and Javonte Green aren't Thompson, but they're active -- especially Holland.

Duren will be out for at least two weeks before his right hamstring strain is evaluated again. Remember, the Pistons no longer have Isaiah Stewart, whom they traded to Memphis in June. Paul Reed has earned a lot of confidence from coach J.B. Bickerstaff and held his own in his matchup against small-ball center LeBron James in Philadelphia on Sunday. The Pistons have looked more mature so far this season. -- Vincent Goodwill

Houston Rockets
BPI chances to make the Finals: 6.1%

Are the Rockets a title contender now that Fred VanVleet is back?

Absolutely. The Houston Rockets won 52 games last season without VanVleet, who suffered a season-ending torn ACL before the start of training camp. With VanVleet out, Houston employed a point guard-by-committee approach that sped up the development of Amen Thompson and Reed Sheppard while enhancing the skill sets of Jabari Smith Jr., Alperen Sengun and Tari Eason.

With VanVleet back in the fold, all those players can naturally slide back into defined roles. VanVleet won't play in back-to-backs during the early part of the season, but Houston smartly added veteran guard Marcus Smart in the offseason to fill the void along with a more developed Sheppard. -- Michael C. Wright

Los Angeles Lakers
BPI chances to make the Finals: 2.9%

Are the Lakers for real after this 3-0 start?

L.A. has the No. 1 offensive rating in the league through its first three games, scoring 125.9 points per 100 possessions. Luka Doncic is averaging 34.3 points, a tick above his 33.5 average last season that earned him his second scoring title. Austin Reaves is averaging 26.7 points, which would be a career high, on a ridiculous 60/60/90 shooting clip. Walker Kessler has made 23 of his first 28 shots and leads the league in field goal percentage (82.1%) and percentage of his points that come in the paint (92%). The Lakers' offense is humming better than an a cappella group.

But L.A.'s defense hasn't shown anything yet. The Lakers rank 16th in defensive rating, allowing 112.4 points per 100 possessions. Yes, that is an improvement from last season, when they allowed 115.5 per 100 possessions. But their wins this season have come against the Golden State Warriors, LA Clippers and Utah Jazz, who are a combined 2-7 to start the season. And the Lakers had to surge back from an 18-point deficit and rely on a 52-point night from Doncic after allowing the Jazz to score 47 in the first quarter. The Lakers' awesome offense won't be enough on its own to carry them as the competition stiffens. -- Dave McMenamin

Minnesota Timberwolves
BPI chances to make the Finals: 14.7%

What's the ceiling on the LaMelo Ball experiment?

The good vibes coming out of training camp have turned into positive results for the Timberwolves to start the season. Ball has been exactly what they've needed. Edwards looks primed for the best offensive season of his career, Ball's passing has made the offense more efficient and Minnesota hasn't had to sacrifice anything on the other end of the floor, leading the league in defensive efficiency entering Monday.

So far, so good, but how far can this carry the Wolves? They look like a legit contender in the West, where San Antonio has stumbled out of the gate with some offensive issues to clean up and Oklahoma City just lost one of its best players to a serious injury. Is it possible Edwards could continue on this trajectory and get into MVP conversations by season's end? Ball's first few games have opened the door to possibilities for this Wolves season. -- Collier

New York Knicks
BPI chances to make the Finals: 11.9%

Are the Knicks experiencing a championship hangover?

Whether it's contract extensions or championship rings, nothing has gone smoothly at 33rd and 8th in Manhattan. The Knicks, who ran through the playoffs, are 30th in offensive efficiency. They have had trouble building leads, let alone sustaining them, most recently blowing a 10-point fourth-quarter cushion to the Paolo Banchero-less Magic.

Hardly anyone for New York is playing up to standard, save for Karl-Anthony Towns. The Knicks are shooting 32% from 3 and 41% overall. Bridges is averaging 3.3 points on 21.7% shooting -- something he's likely to shake out of but still worth noting. Eventually, things will turn, but Mike Brown put it bluntly: "Our crap stinks, it does." -- Goodwill

Oklahoma City Thunder
BPI chances to make the Finals: 45.5%

How can the Thunder overcome another devastating injury?

Unfortunately, Oklahoma City has a lot of experience in adjusting to the absences of its core players. A fractured pelvis sidelined Chet Holmgren for three months in 2024-25, when the Thunder won 68 games and made a championship run after the 7-footer returned to the lineup following the trade deadline. A series of injuries limited Jalen Williams to only 33 games last season, and recurring hamstring issues sidelined him for most of the playoffs, a major factor in the Thunder failing to repeat.

Now, the Thunder will be without Williams again for the foreseeable future after he suffered a gruesome ankle injury. Even after the offseason departures of key role players Luguentz Dort, Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins, Oklahoma City has one of the league's deepest rosters. But the Thunder lack big wings aside from Williams, and his defensive versatility will be especially missed. -- MacMahon

Philadelphia 76ers
BPI chances to make the Finals: 22.6%

Is it time to worry about the Sixers' front court depth?

Yes, but it seems that help is on the way. The Sixers' front court has been decimated to begin the season. They have two injured big men who haven't played a game: Dominick Barlow (back) and Tacko Fall (quad). Another two have missed time to start the season: Dean Wade, who missed the opening two games because of a left ankle sprain, and Jabari Walker, who exited the Sixers' third game because of a left knee injury and missed their last loss to the Pistons.

It means a lot of small-ball lineups with LeBron James playing center -- a role James isn't hoping to fill often -- and the Sixers being significantly outrebounded. They've been outrebounded in every game this season, and by an average of 19.5 over their past two outings. Joel Embiid and Adem Bona are currently the team's only healthy centers, but the Sixers are hoping Barlow, Walker and Fall return soon. -- Kris Rhim

San Antonio Spurs
BPI chances to make the Finals: 24.8%

Have the Spurs regressed from NBA Finals form?

Spurs coach Mitch Johnson made the gutsy call to push forward the evolution of a new starting lineup. Finals standout Dylan Harper joins last season's starting lineup, alongside fellow guards Stephon Castle and De'Aaron Fox. Johnson knew the three-guard lineup would create some growing pains.

"I understand the frustrations and the tension of it. But I do believe the players and staff have, whether it's put in the thought and time to feel comfortable about what we're committing to, and then also the patience to allow things to grow organically and how they need to be to get to where they want to get to in terms of on-the-job reps, on-the-job experience against the best teams in the world in this league," Johnson said. -- Wright

Toronto Raptors
BPI chances to make the Finals: 8.0%

What has Kawhi Leonard's early impact been on the Raptors?

The Kawhi experience is already in effect. He played in the first two games -- although not that well by his standards, especially shooting the ball -- and the Raptors won both games by a combined 53 points. OK, this was because they destroyed the Bulls by 43 in the opener, and it warped everything.

Anyway, Leonard was a late scratch Sunday because of swelling in his left knee, and it sounded like he was headed for imaging Monday. The Raptors were promptly blown out in Minnesota, with Scottie Barnes going 0-of-12 from the floor in a miserable night without Leonard.

It's worth pointing out that Leonard's knee issues have largely been on his right side, where he has had at least three surgeries. This latest issue is affecting his "good" knee. But the fact that Leonard is already missing time with a worrisome knee issue in the first week of the season is a developing story. And probably predictable. -- Windhorst

Formula 1 heads to Mexico on a weekend where Kimi Antonelli could win the drivers' championship for the first time.

The Mercedes driver extended his lead in the title to 123 points from George Russell after winning the United States Grand Prix. He will simply need to finish ninth or higher in Mexico City to seal the title.

Ferrari's Charles Leclerc was looking strong in the upgraded Ferrari to finish second in Austin, with Max Verstappen on the final step of the podium.

Mexico City is one of the most vibrant atmospheres on the calendar and fans congregate in the thousands to cheer on home hero Sergio Pérez.

It's a true anomaly on the calendar due to the high altitude of of 7,300 feet (2,200 metres) and therefore presents a unique challenge for the teams and drivers. Teams can run Monaco-level downforce packages while still reaching Monza-esque top speeds.

Antonelli put his Mercedes on a surprise pole in Austin and converted it into another victory as he inches closer to taking the title crown with five races remaining.

The youngster will need just two points this weekend, or for Russell and Hamilton to not win the race, to get the job done in Mexico.

Red Bull are a looming threat each weekend after bringing major upgrades and Verstappen will be one to watch out for. He's also got five race victories under his belt around Mexico City.

All eyes will be on Antonelli. He will be hoping to wrap up the title and is looking like he's in a position where nobody will be able to stop him.

stories.headline: Smesko rips refs for 'ridiculous' missed calls on Reese in Game 5 of WNBA Finals
stories.summary: Dream head coach Karl Smesko blasted refs for missing what he called a "ridiculous" amount of contact on Angel Reese in Monday night's Game 5 loss.
stories.body:
SAN FRANCISCO -- Atlanta Dream coach Karl Smesko stood defiantly behind star Angel Reese on Monday night, criticizing officials for missing what he called a "ridiculous" amount of contact in Monday night's 64-55 loss to the Golden State Valkyries in Game 5 of the WNBA Finals.

Reese finished with seven points on 2-of-8 shooting and went 3-of-4 from the free throw line in the loss, which put Atlanta in a 3-2 series hole.

"I give [the Valkyries] credit for playing good defense, they're known for their defense," Smesko said. "But I want to have Angel's back here. The contact on Angel compared to everybody else is just ridiculous. Just ridiculous."

He added about the officiating: "You can't be at this level and make that many mistakes."

Smesko's main point of contention was what he felt to be a number of missed calls against Reese. He also said he felt there were a number of missed double dribbles and travel calls against the Valkyries.

Reese shared in the frustration, saying the physical play and questionable officiating have been a recurring theme for her this year.

"I am still trying to figure out how to play through the physicality," said Reese, who was also called for four personal fouls. "I'm kind of used to it because this was happening throughout the season, so I have to just continue to play through it. But honestly, for my teammates, when they're getting slapped to the floor or knocked off, it's a little frustrating."

She continued: "I know I have the mismatch, especially talking about matchups. So when I do switch on the post and I'm a lot stronger than the opponent, I should be able to turn and they're calling an offensive foul. But when I'm getting pushed before that, it's frustrating to me."

It's the first time in Reese's career she has had consecutive games with two or fewer field goals, in the regular season or postseason, and just the second time she has been held to single-digit scoring in consecutive games (2024).

In Game 4, Reese had eight points on 2-of-12 shooting and hit four of her six attempted free throws. She was also called for four fouls in that game.

Reese said she felt a shift in officiating in Game 4.

Atlanta took 116 free throws in the first four games (29.0 per game). In Games 2, 3 and 4, the Dream became the second team to attempt at least 25 free throws in three straight Finals games in WNBA history, according to ESPN Insights.

As a team, the Dream shot 11-of-14 from the free throw line Monday, the fewest free throw attempts they've had in a game this postseason. It's tied for their second fewest in any game this season.

"It definitely shifted when we went up 2-1," Reese said. "I don't know what happened, but it definitely took a big turn."

Overall, Game 5 was a historically bad scoring night for both teams. The Valkyries' 64 points were the fewest in a Finals win since the Sacramento Monarchs in 2005, and the Dream's 55 were the fewest in a Finals game since the Mercury in Game 3 of the 2021 Finals.

Atlanta hit just 29.2% of their shots, the fourth lowest by any team in a WNBA Finals game, and just 23.5% in the paint, the worst by any team in a game this postseason.

"There are things that are on us, like we're missing shots we should make. But at the same time, that needs to be a whole lot better than it was," Smesko said. "It you push someone with two hands, that's got to be a foul. I'm kind of tired of some of the excuses that I'm hearing."

Meanwhile, Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase said this level of physicality is expected at this stage of the Finals and series.

"Both teams really want to win this," Nakase said. "These are two defensive-minded teams ... they like physicality, so that's part of it. I ain't shocked about this. You have an Atlanta Dream team that's well-coached, that have dogs, same as us."

stories.headline: Bayern Munich's Vincent Kompany 'stable,' could be away for weeks after collapse
stories.summary: Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany will have more tests to determine why he collapsed during a training session the previous day, the club said Saturday.
stories.body:
Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany will undergo more testing to determine why he collapsed during a training session the previous day, the club said Saturday.

Board member for sport Max Eberl told reporters that Kompany's condition was "stable" and that doctors were focused on "trying to find out" the cause.

"The tests have already yielded some results, but further results are needed to determine exactly what it is and how long it will take for him to recover," Eberl said.

Kompany, 40, was observing a training session for the reserves team when the incident occurred Friday.

Kompany had been dealing with a viral infection since last week, and his assistant Aaron Danks said on Tuesday it affected the Belgian's legs.

Kompany remained seated throughout Bayern's 6-1 win over Leipzig last week and then missed a training session and a pregame news conference on Tuesday, when Danks said he needed time to rest at home.

However, Kompany returned to the dugout for Wednesday's 2-2 draw against Arsenal in the Champions League. Following that match, Kompany acknowledged he tried to push through the illness and failed to heed the signals from his body.

Eberl said that he spoke to Kompany and his wife on Friday after Kompany collapsed.

- Bayern's Kompany hospitalized after collapsing at training

The executive added that as of now there was no time frame for when Kompany would return, saying it could take weeks.

"He'll only come back when he's fit," Eberl said. "We're not going to start setting any time frames. We need to find out what the issue is, and then it's a question of what the recovery time will be. We're not talking in terms of days, but weeks."

Kompany, a former player, joined Bayern in 2024 from Burnley and has won the German league twice since then. Kompany's team also reached the Champions League semifinals and won the German Cup last season.

He is nominated for the Johan Cruyff Trophy for the best coach of the year to be announced Monday.

Bayern will visit Freiburg in the Bundesliga on Sunday.

stories.headline: Consensus top AFL draft prospect Dougie Cochrane already in rare air
stories.summary: Missing significant chunks of football hasn't stopped Port Adelaide NGA star Dougie Cochrane from firming as the top prospect in this year's AFL Draft.
stories.body:
It's rare for a player to be the consensus no. 1 rated prospect in their draft. From coaches to recruiters and a myriad of draft evaluators, Dougie Cochrane stands atop 2026's crop. For him to do so after playing just four games in his top-age campaign puts the Port Adelaide NGA gun in rare air.

The starring junior missed both years of his u18 national championships through injury, and this year only returned to the field in the final month of the season. But what he produced at league level last season and amongst his peers at the u16s national championships in 2024 is not easily forgotten.

Clearly a class above at the national championships three years ago, Cochrane put all of his skill and athleticism on show. He was a distributor out of defence, won aerial duels around the ground and was the focal point of the SA forward line in a showing of his unique versatility.

From there he made his league debut for Central Districts as a 17-year-old, kicking four goals including an outrageous snap on his left foot from the pocket after crumbing a forward 50 contest. From his first game he was already the best player on the ground.

Speaking to ESPN ahead of the draft combine Cochrane was a bit flat. It wasn't because he'd missed his top-age season, he knew he wasn't going to be testing, and he knew most clubs wouldn't bother booking an interview given his ties to Port Adelaide. But there was one thing that really got to him.

"They measured me at 194-and-a-half centimetres," he tells ESPN with a grin. "They took a centimetre off me, but we'll round that up."

At six-foot-four (we'll round it up too) he's widely considered the next elite key forward prospect to come through the AFL Draft. Only he doesn't necessarily see it that way.

"I want to be a midfielder when I'm older, that's what I'm striving towards. "For right now I'm pretty happy forward, if not back. I'm happy wherever the team needs, whatever the team needs.

"I'm pretty skinny right now, I'm not as muscly as the Patty Cripps's of the world, the Bonts of the world. I want to focus on my midfield craft and get that experience."

Cochrane missed a significant chunk of his bottom-age year with a hamstring and over the off-season underwent knee surgery to address patella tendinitis. He didn't play for 11 straight months from the end of 2025 to July 2026.

Watching from the sidelines frustrated him but he knew it was all out of an abundance of caution.

"I started playing league at Centrals last year, I sort of started feeling [knee pain] a little bit. I thought nothing of it, just thought it was a bit of growing pain. It got worse and worse by the time I started doing pre-season... when you take off and do your powerful stuff it flares up.

"They did a clean out of it... I had the surgery, and I walked out of the surgery. It was two little key holes."

Cochrane sat down with ESPN as Port Adelaide list manager Jason Cripps all but confirmed on Trade Radio Essendon would be bidding on the gun academy prospect at pick one in the 2026 AFL Draft.

He's the son of Port Adelaide and North Melbourne midfielder Stuart Cochrane, and grew up supporting the Power after his dad's playing career finished up. His brother Tom was on the list during formative years and the club is set up to match his bid wherever it lands.

"Dad's been my idol growing up. Looking up to him, I obviously didn't get to see him play but he's been enormous."

Asked if it would mean more being that first selection on November 19, Cochrane's humble nature shines through.

"I loved watching the draft growing up, seeing those high picks. The pick doesn't really matter, does it? There have been a lot of picks over times where the number one picks haven't gone as well as they should've. I just want to end up at an AFL club - wherever that is I don't mind - but I just want to play footy," he says.

"Growing up and supporting Port all my life, it would be special playing for them. But whatever happens happens and I'm just gonna let that decide itself."
